T: A1 to enjoy or approve of something or someone
› to show that you think something is good on a social networking website by clicking on a symbol or the word 'like'
A1 used to say politely that you want something

NONE: A2 similar to; in the same way or manner as
B1 in a way that suggests
為…所特有的，符合…特點的
› used before you describe how you were feeling or what you said when something happened to you
（用於引出自己對已發生事件的感覺或想法）
› used in conversation as a pause or to emphasize an adjective
（用於對話中表示停頓或強調形容詞）
› also the likes of sb/sth a person, thing, or group similar in character or quality to the one mentioned
› not for the type of people mentioned
不是為…之類的人準備的

C: › [ C ] (on a page on a social networking website) an act of showing that you think something is good by clicking a button

NONE: › to be likely to do something

example: I like your new haircut.
我喜歡你的新髮型。
Do you like fish?
你愛吃魚嗎？
I like it when a book is so good that you can't put it down.
我喜歡那種碰上好書時手不釋卷的感覺。
I quite like wine but I could live without it.
我很喜歡喝酒，但沒有酒我還是可以忍受的。
He's very well-liked (= popular) at work.
他在工作中人緣相當好。
I like the way he just assumes we'll listen to him when he doesn't take in a word anyone else says! (= I don't like it and it annoys me.)
他誰的話都聽不進去，卻以為我們大家都會聽他的，對此我非常反感。
[ + -ing verb ] I don't like upsetting people.
我不喜歡搞得別人心煩意亂。
[ + to infinitive ] He likes to spend his evenings in front of the television.
他喜歡晚上看電視消磨時間。
[ + past participle ] He likes his steak well-done.
他喜歡吃熟透的牛排。
Like us on Facebook!
在臉書上給我們加讚吧！
More than 200 people liked my post.
超過200人為我的文章加讚了。
I think I'd like the soup for my starter.
我想要一份湯做頭盤。
I'd like to go to Moscow.
我想去莫斯科。
I would like to say a big thank you to everyone who's helped to make our wedding such a special occasion!
我想對參與籌備我們婚禮的每一個人表示由衷的感謝，正是你們讓這個婚禮如此與眾不同！
I'd like one of the round loaves, please.
請給我拿一個圓麵包。
[ + to infinitive ] I'd like to book a seat for tonight's performance.
我想預訂一個今晚演出的座位。
[ + obj + to infinitive ] I'd like you to send this for me, please.
請你幫我把這個寄出。
[ + past participle ] I would like the whole lot finished by the weekend.
我希望這些工作能在週末前做完。
He looks like his brother.
他長得像他哥哥。
She's very much like her mother (= she is similar in appearance or character).
她和她母親非常像。
Is Japanese food like Chinese?
日本料理和中餐相似嗎？
I've got a sweater just like that.
我有一件和那件一模一樣的毛衣。
Her hair was so soft it was like silk.
她的頭髮如絲綢般柔順。
You're acting like a complete idiot!
你的舉動像個十足的白癡！
She sings like an angel!
她的歌聲如天使一般！
Like I said (= as I have already said), I don't wear perfume.
我說過了，我不用香水。
Like most people (= as most people would), I'd prefer to have enough money not to work.
和大多數人一樣，我喜歡能有足夠的錢而不必去工作。
It feels/seems like (= it seems to me) ages since we last spoke.
我們好像很久沒有說過話了。
There's nothing like a good cup of coffee (= it's better than anything)!
任何東西都比不了一杯好咖啡！

It looks like I'm going to be in the office until late tonight.
看起來我得到深夜才能離開辦公室了。
It looks like rain (= I think it is going to rain).
我看天要下雨了。
It sounds to me like you ought to change jobs.
聽起來你似乎應該換個工作。
You look like you've just got out of bed!
你看起來好像剛剛起床！
not standard She acts like she's stupid!
她似乎總做傻事！
That's just like Maisie to turn up half an hour late to her own party!
梅茜就是這樣的人，為她辦派對時她都要拖後半小時才露面！
It's not like you to be so quiet - are you all right, my love?
你平時沒這麽安靜呀——親愛的，你沒事吧？
She looks best in bright, vibrant colours, like red and pink.
她穿鮮亮顔色的衣服最漂亮，如紅色和粉色。
Then I saw how late it was and I'm like, so upset.
然後我才明白已經很晚了，因此感覺特別沮喪。
He started shouting at me and I'm like, "What's your problem? I'm on your side!"
他開始朝我大喊大叫起來，於是我就問他：「你怎麽回事？我是站在你這邊的！」
He's, like, really friendly - someone you can talk to.
他呀，真的非常友善——就是那種可以傾心交談的人。
If there's nothing you can do to change the situation, it's like - why bother?
如果你無法改變這種局面，那麽幹嗎去費這個神呢？
Boxing hasn't seen the likes of Muhammad Ali since he retired.
穆罕默德·阿里退役後，拳擊運動就再也沒有他那樣的選手了。
He was a very great actor - we won't see his like again.
他是個非常了不起的演員——沒有人能達到他那樣的水準。
He described a superlative meal, the like of which he'd never eaten before.
他說那頓飯特別美味，他從未吃過如此好吃的飯。
They're competing with the likes of Microsoft.
他們在跟微軟這樣的公司競爭。
There's a big sports hall for tennis and badminton and such like.
那裡有一個可供網球、羽毛球等比賽用的大型體育館。
The star lists his likes as "my new Porsche, my girlfriend, and staying up all night."
這個流行歌星說他的最愛是「我的保時捷新車、女友和徹夜狂歡」。
They can't expect me to accommodate all their silly little likes and dislikes.
他們別指望我能容忍他們所有那些愚蠢可笑、無足輕重的個人好惡。
First-class travel is for rich people - it's not for the likes of us.
頭等艙是供上層人士使用的——不是給我們這樣的人準備的。
My new profile picture got 100 likes.
我的新頭像圖片得到了100個贊。
The paper criticized what it described as the animal-like behaviour of the fans.
該報批評了球迷們的表現，稱之為野蠻行為。
There was a large, ball-like structure on top of the building.
大樓的頂部有一個球型構造物。
childlike trust
像孩子一樣天真地信賴某人
a cabbage-like vegetable
一種像甘藍菜的蔬菜

NONE: › If someone is like a bull in a china shop, they are very careless in the way that they move or behave.
笨手笨腳的人；魯莽闖禍的人

example: We told her it was a delicate situation but she went into the meeting like a bull in a china shop.
我們告訴她情況非常微妙，但她開會時還是冒冒失失的。

NONE: › used to describe someone who is in a state of extreme nervous worry
如熱鍋上的螞蟻，坐立不安

example: The medicine went through me like a dose of salts.
這種藥物很快就從我體內排出了。

NONE: › If someone does something or goes somewhere like a lamb to the slaughter, they do it without knowing that something bad is going to happen and therefore act calmly and without fighting against the situation.
› in a wild and uncontrolled way

example: He's been running around the office this morning like a man possessed.
他今天上午一直在辦公室裡跑來跑去，像個瘋子似的。

NONE: › UK If someone works like a maniac, they work extremely hard.
（工作或鍛煉）狂熱地，極其努力地
› When someone does something like a shot, they do it extremely quickly and enthusiastically.

example: The moment I let go of the dog, she's off like a shot.
我一放開那隻狗，牠就飛快地跑掉了。
She grabbed the money and ran out of the shop like a streak of lightning.
她一把抓起錢，飛也似的跑出商店。

NONE: › secretly or unexpectedly and without being seen

example: If Dad finds out what you've been doing, he'll come down on (= punish) you like a ton of bricks!
如果爸爸知道你在做的事，他會狠狠教訓你的！

NONE: › very regularly, or at exactly the planned times

example: Since the recent improvements to the service, the buses are running like clockwork.
最近，自從改善服務後，公車運行得非常準時。
My daughter always calls me every Friday evening, (as) regular as clockwork.
我女兒總是每星期五晚上給我打電話，非常準時。

NONE: B2 If you do something like crazy, you do a lot of it or do it very quickly.
發瘋似的；拼命地；飛快地

example: They were working like crazy to get the job done on time.
爲了按時完工，他們在拼命工作。

NONE: › used to describe a drink or liquid that is unpleasant because it contains too much water and has very little flavour
（指飲料等淡而無味）像洗碗水一樣

example: This soup/tea tastes like dishwater.
這湯／茶像洗碗水一樣淡而無味。
I've been working like fury these past few days to catch up.
過去的這幾天裡我一直奮力工作以求趕上進度。

NONE: › said about something that is very difficult to get because a lot of people want it

example: Tickets for the concert are like gold dust.
這場音樂會真是一票難求。
As soon as I mentioned work, he was out of the door like greased lightning!
我剛一提到工作的事，他就一溜煙似的跑出去了！
We ran like hell.
我們拼命地跑。
We worked like hell to finish the job.
我們為完成工作而拼命地做。
It hurt like hell.
痛得要命。
"Try to be polite to him." "Like hell I will!"
「對他禮貌點。」「我才不呢！」

NONE: › If you tell someone to like it or lump it, you mean that person must accept a situation they do not like, because it cannot be changed.
必須接受某個現狀，因為情況沒法改變

example: Like it or lump it, romantic fiction is read regularly by thousands.
還是接受現實吧，數以千計的人都有讀言情小說的習慣。

NONE: › in a silly way, without thinking, and in large numbers

example: People rushed like lemmings to invest in the company.
人們一窩蜂地把錢投進了該公司。

NONE: B2 If you do something like mad, you do it very enthusiastically, quickly, or a lot.

example: She's been saving like mad because she wants to buy a car.
她想買汽車，所以在拚命存錢。
He was scribbling away like nobody's business.
他忙著寫個不停。

NONE: 極其古怪；極不尋常；非常糟糕

example: With his make-up and strange clothes, he looked like nothing on earth.
他化了妝，穿了一身稀奇古怪的衣服，看上去像個外星人。

NONE: › very strange, unusual, or unpleasant in appearance, sound, or taste
（外觀、聲音或味道）非常怪異的，與眾不同的，令人生厭的

example: It looked nice, but it tasted like nothing on earth.
它看起來不錯，但味道卻很怪異。

NONE: › If you say that making someone do something was like pulling teeth, you mean it was very difficult and they did not want to do it.

example: Getting her to tell me about her childhood was like pulling teeth.
請她告訴我她的童年往事是一件十分艱難的事情。

NONE: › If two people are like ships that pass in the night, they meet once or twice by chance for a short time then do not see each other again.
› If someone works like stink, they work extremely hard.

example: You'll have to run like the clappers if you want to catch your train.
要是你想趕上火車就得飛奔。

NONE: › If someone does something like there is/was no tomorrow, they do it very fast, in large amounts and without thinking carefully.
好像沒有將來似的；不顧一切地

example: After he won the lottery, he began spending money like there was no tomorrow.
他贏了彩票後，開始拼命花錢。
The twins are like two peas in a pod.
那對雙胞胎長得極像。

NONE: C2 criticisms of or warnings to a particular person that have no effect on that person
（批評或警誡對某人）像水過鴨背，毫無影響，不起作用

example: I've told him that he's heading for trouble, but he doesn't listen - it's just water off a duck's back.
我已經告訴過他會有麻煩，可是他不聽——說了也白說，根本毫無作用。

NONE: › People who are described as like-minded share the same opinions, ideas, or interests.
意見相同的，想法一致的；興趣相投的

example: A dedicated football fan herself, she started the magazine for like-minded women.
作為一位忠實的足球迷，她為興趣相投的女性創辦了這份雜誌。

NONE: › A likeable person is pleasant and easy to like.

example: He's a very likeable sort of bloke.
他是那種非常討人喜歡的傢夥。

NONE: C2 the chance that something will happen

example: This latest dispute greatly increases the likelihood of a strike.
最近的這場衝突極大地增加了罷工的可能性。
[ + that ] There is every likelihood that more jobs will be lost later this year.
今年晚些時候很可能會有更多的人失業。
There is little likelihood now that interest rates will come down further.
現在利率進一步下降的可能性幾乎爲零。
In all likelihood everything will go to plan.
一切幾乎肯定會按計劃進行。

NONE: B1 If something is likely, it will probably happen or is expected.
很可能的，可能要發生的

example: Do remind me because I'm likely to forget.
一定要提醒我，因爲我可能會忘記。
What's the likely outcome of this whole business?
整宗事件可能會出現甚麽結果？
I suppose that might happen but it's not very likely.
我認為那樣的事也許會發生，但可能性不大。
[ + that ] It's quite likely that we'll be in Spain this time next year.
明年的這個時候我們很可能會在西班牙。
Opposite
unlikely
She will likely need surgery.
她有可能需要動手術。
As likely as not, she'll end up in court over this problem.
關於這個問題她最終很可能會訴諸法律。
Most likely he'll turn up late.
not likely!

NONE: › to say that someone is similar to or has the same qualities as someone else

example: She's been likened to a young Elizabeth Taylor.
人們說她很像年輕時的伊麗莎白‧泰勒。

NONE: › the fact of being similar in appearance
› a painting or other image of a person that looks very like them
（人物肖像作品等）非常逼真，極其相像

example: There's a definite family likeness around the eyes.
很明顯這家人眼睛長得都很像。
Just water these plants twice a week, and likewise the ones in the bedroom.
這些植物一周澆兩次水，臥室裡的那些也一樣。
informal "I don't have time to spend hours preparing one dish!" "Likewise (= it's the same for me)."
「我沒有功夫花好幾個小時去做一個菜！」「我也一樣。」

NONE: › a feeling that you like someone or something; the fact of liking someone or something

example: She has a liking for fine wines.
她喜歡好酒。
I'm developing quite a liking for jazz.
我漸漸喜歡上了爵士樂。
The dessert was too sweet for my liking (= I like it less sweet).
按我的口味，這個甜品有點甜了。
formal Is the room to your liking, Sir (= are you satisfied with it)?
先生，您對這個房間滿意嗎？
